sections.title: Identification and form
sections.text: The catalogue entry represents Pinus sylvestris, Scots pine, rather than the whole genus. This Eurasian conifer usually reaches 30–35 m and can exceed 40 m.

sections.title: Needles, bark and cones
sections.text: The slightly twisted blue-green needles grow in pairs and are about 4–7 cm long. The bark on the upper trunk is often orange. The hanging cones are about 3–6 cm long and release winged seeds.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: The wood is used as timber. No specific human food use is included here.
